\caption{Results across the closure matrix: the three financing closures (rows)
crossed with the five labour-market closures (columns). Each cell reports the
change in real GDP ($\Delta Y$), employment ($\Delta L$), the price level
($\Delta P$, the GDP deflator), the net external position
($\Delta D = R + B_{\mathrm{gov}}$, the external-account block; positive = net external
financing received, i.e.\ external debt) and household consumption welfare
($\Delta W$), all in percent against the reference continuation. Generated from the
\texttt{matrix\_5x3-v10-*} run manifests; no number is hand-typed. The
elastic-supply column is the sectoral closure at four uniform supply elasticities,
$\eta_{s,i} \in \{0.25, 0.5, 1, 2\}$ (\texttt{matrix\_5x3-v10-BETA-F*-etas025},
\dots, \texttt{-etas2}); $\eta_{s,i} = 0.5$ (bold) is the headline value used in
the text. The fixed-wage and Leontief columns
coincide (bit-identical), and F2 and F3 coincide in the three flexible-wage
columns, so at the headline elasticity the fifteen cells describe nine distinct economies: the standard-CGE
column is exactly output-neutral, and equilibrium prices move away from the
baseline only in the two sectoral-wage columns (no reallocation, elastic supply).}
\label{tab:results-matrix}
\end{table}
